345184.title: The pendant-vertex conjecture for local antimagic chromatic number of trees
345184.statement: Let $T_k$ be a tree with $k\ge 2$ pendant vertices. Caterpillars, spiders, and lobsters are standard classes of trees, and $\chi_{la}(T_k)$ denotes the local antimagic chromatic number of $T_k$. **Pendant-vertex conjecture.** Every tree $T_k$, other than certain caterpillars, spiders and lobsters, with $k\ge 2$ pendant vertices has $\chi_{la}(T_k)=k+1$. This proposes that the lower bound furnished by the pendant vertices is attained for all but specified exceptional tree families; the paper does not characterize the exceptional families or establish the assertion in general.

345351.title: Wang's arbitrary directed W-cycle-factor conjecture
345351.statement:
Let $D$ be a digraph of order $n\geq 6$, and let $W\subseteq V(D)$. An **arbitrary $W$-cycle-factor** is a collection of disjoint directed cycles realizing a prescribed partition of $|W|$ into parts of size at least $2$.

**Wang's conjecture.** If $\delta(W)\geq (3n-3)/2$, then $D$ contains an arbitrary $W$-cycle-factor.

This conjecture generalizes Wang's directed arbitrary cycle-factor conjecture and the graph version for specified vertex sets. Its status is not established in the source.

345827.title: Induced-subgraph family conjecture for gap-free graphs
345827.statement:
For each integer $n\geq2$, consider families of graphs $\{G_i^{(n)}\}$. A graph is **gap-free** when it has no induced subgraph consisting of two disjoint edges, and $I(G)$ denotes its edge ideal.

**Induced-subgraph family conjecture.** For all integers $n\geq2$, there exists a family of graphs $\{G_i^{(n)}\}$ such that $I(G_i^{(n)})^k$ has a linear resolution for all $k\geq n-1$, and whenever $G$ is a gap-free graph with $\reg(I(G))=n$, each $G_i^{(n)}$ is an induced subgraph of $G$.

This is proposed as a structural question related to the generalized Nevo–Peeva conjecture: it seeks families of graphs whose powers have the required linear resolutions and that occur inside every gap-free graph with the specified regularity. The supplied text gives no resolution status.

346167.title: The rainbow vertex-disconnection Nordhaus–Gaddum conjecture
346167.statement:
Let $G$ and $\overline{G}$ be nontrivial connected graphs of order $n\geq 8$. Write $rvd(G)$ for the rainbow vertex-disconnection number of $G$. **Rainbow vertex-disconnection Nordhaus–Gaddum conjecture.**

$$
rvd(G)+rvd(\overline{G})\geq n.
$$

This conjecture proposes an improvement of the established lower bound for the sum of the rainbow vertex-disconnection numbers of a graph and its complement. The paper notes that the bound holds when $rvd(G)=1$, but does not establish it for all nontrivial connected graphs of order at least $8$.

346763.title: Generalized Sidon-set existence conjecture for perfect powers
346763.statement:
Let $k\geq 1$, $h\geq 2$, and $\varepsilon>0$. A **$B_h[g]$ set** $A\subseteq(\mathbb{Z}^{+})^k$ is a set of $k$-th powers with counting function $A(x)$. **Generalized Sidon-set conjecture.** For every $k\geq 1$, $h\geq 2$, and $\varepsilon>0$, there exists a $B_h[g]$ set $A\subseteq(\mathbb{Z}^{+})^k$ such that

$$
A(x)\gg x^{\min\left\{\frac{1}{k},\frac{1}{h}\right\}-\varepsilon}.
$$

The exponent is optimal up to the factor $x^{-\varepsilon}$ because every such set satisfies $A(x)\ll x^{\min\{1/k,1/h\}}$. The conjecture was proved for $k=1$ and all $h\geq2$, and the cited results also imply the case $k=h=2$; the general assertion remains unresolved in the source.

346921.title: An upper-threshold conjecture for extremal beta-free words over the binary alphabet
346921.statement: Let $w$ be a word over the binary alphabet $\Sigma_2$. For $\beta\in\mathbb{R}_{\text{ext}}$, call $w$ **extremal $\beta$-free** if it is $\beta$-free and every extension of $w$ contains a factor of exponent at least $\beta$. Here, a word is $\beta$-free if no factor has exponent greater than or equal to $\beta$. **Binary upper-threshold conjecture.** There is some number $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}_{\text{ext}}$ such that, for every $\beta\in\mathbb{R}_{\text{ext}}$ with $\beta\geq\alpha$, there are no extremal $\beta$-free words over $\Sigma_2$. This asks whether the binary extremal problem eventually has a negative answer as the exponent threshold increases; the source establishes existence for $2^+\leq\beta\leq 8/3$, while the problem remains open for $\beta\geq 8/3^+$.

346984.title: Qin–Xu–Zhou's conjecture on nontrivially unstable circulants of odd order
346984.statement: Let $X$ be a circulant, that is, a Cayley graph on a cyclic group. Its canonical double cover $B(X)$ is the bipartite graph with vertex set $V(X)\times\mathbb{Z}_2$ in which $(x,0)$ is adjacent to $(y,1)$ exactly when $x$ and $y$ are adjacent in $X$. The graph $X$ is **unstable** if $B(X)$ has automorphisms that do not preserve the two canonical bipartition classes, and **nontrivially unstable** if it is unstable without belonging to the trivial exceptional class described in the source. **Qin–Xu–Zhou's conjecture.** There is no nontrivially unstable circulant of odd order. This conjecture concerns the classification of vertex-transitive unstable graphs. It is known that every circulant of odd prime order is stable, but the assertion for all odd orders remains open.

347033.title: Berkovich–Uncu's eventual positivity conjecture for $H_{L,s,k}(q)$
347033.statement:
For positive integers $n\geq 1$, define the $q$-Pochhammer symbol by

$$
(a;q)_n=(1-a)(1-aq)\cdots(1-aq^{n-1}),
$$

with $(a;q)_0=1$. For positive integers $L$, $s$, and $k$, define

$$
H_{L,s,k}(q)=\frac{q^s(1-q^k)}{(q^s;q)_{L+1}}-\left(\frac{1}{(q^{s+1};q)_L}-1\right).
$$

A series $\sum_{n\geq 0}a_nq^n$ is **eventually positive** if there is an $l\in\mathbb N$ such that $a_n>0$ for all $n\geq l$. **Berkovich and Uncu's conjecture.** For positive integers $L$, $s$, and $k$ with $L\geq 3$ and $k\geq s+1$, the series $H_{L,s,k}(q)$ is eventually positive. The supplied context does not state whether this conjecture is resolved.

347489.title: The finite-colour Seurat game conjecture for digraphs
347489.statement:
Let ${\bf G}^n(G,H)$ be the Seurat game with $n$ colours played on digraphs $G$ and $H$, with players $\forall$ and $\exists$, where $\forall$ seeks to distinguish non-isomorphic digraphs and $\exists$ seeks to match the colouring moves. **Seurat game conjecture.** There is $n\geq 2$ such that for all digraphs $G,H$, if $G\not\cong H$ then $\forall$ has a winning strategy in

$$
{\bf G}^n(G,H).
$$

If true, this would say that a fixed finite number of colours suffices to distinguish every pair of non-isomorphic digraphs in these games; the source describes the question as open and notes that no pair of non-isomorphic graphs is known on which $\exists$ can avoid losing even with two colours.

347559.title: Strict paired domination inequality for direct products of trees
347559.statement:
Let $T_1$ and $T_2$ be trees of order at least $2$, and let $\gamma_{\mathrm{pr}}(T)$ denote the paired domination number of a graph $T$. **Strict paired domination conjecture.**

$$
\gamma_{\mathrm{pr}}(T_1 \times T_2) > \frac{1}{2} \gamma_{\mathrm{pr}}(T_1)\gamma_{\mathrm{pr}}(T_2).
$$

The corresponding non-strict inequality with factor $\frac{1}{2}$ is known for all trees, and the conjecture asserts that equality is never attained for trees of order at least $2$.

347594.title: The monotonicity sandwich conjecture for average dominating-set order
347594.statement:
Let $G$ be a nonempty graph. For a vertex $v$ and an edge $e$, write $G-v$ and $G-e$ for the graphs obtained by deleting $v$ and $e$, respectively. **The monotonicity sandwich conjecture.** There exist a vertex $v$ and an edge $e$ such that

$$
\operatorname{avd}(G-v)<\operatorname{avd}(G)<\operatorname{avd}(G-e).
$$

Although deleting a vertex or edge always decreases the number of dominating sets, it need not make the average order of a dominating set monotone in either direction. The conjecture is reported to hold for all graphs on at most $7$ vertices; its validity for all nonempty graphs remains open.

347961.title: The bounded-diameter bipartite monochromatic-cover conjecture
347961.statement:
Let $\mathcal{K}_2$ be the family of complete bipartite graphs. A **monochromatic cover** is a collection of monochromatic connected subgraphs covering all vertices, and its order is its number of subgraphs.

**Bipartite bounded-diameter conjecture.** There is an integer $d$ such that, for every $r\geq 2$, every $r$-coloring of every $K\in\mathcal{K}_2$ has a monochromatic cover of order at most $2r-2$ whose subgraphs all have diameter at most $d$.

The paper proves this for $r=2$ and $r=3; $ the general statement remains open.

347962.title: The tightly connected monochromatic subgraph conjecture for complete uniform hypergraphs
347962.statement:
Let $K_n^r$ denote the complete $r$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices. A **tightly connected** subgraph is one in which every two vertices can be joined by a sequence of edges in which consecutive edges intersect in exactly $r-1$ vertices.

**Tightly connected hypergraph conjecture.** For every $r\geq 3$, every $r$-coloring of $K_n^r$ contains a monochromatic tightly connected subgraph covering all vertices of $K_n^r$.

The paper proves the case $r=3$; the general statement remains open.

348055.title: Kalai–Meshulam total Betti number conjecture for independence complexes
348055.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. Its **independence complex** $\mathrm{Ind}(G)$ is the simplicial complex whose faces are the independent sets of $G$, and let $\beta$ denote its total Betti number. For every induced subgraph $H$ of $G$, consider $\beta(\mathrm{Ind}(H))$.

**Kalai–Meshulam total Betti number conjecture.** For any graph $G$, we have

$$
\beta(\mathrm{Ind}(H)) \leq 1
$$

for every induced subgraph $H$ of $G$ if and only if there are no induced cycles of length divisible by three in $G$.

The source states that this conjecture remains open. It is a stronger topological analogue of the reduced Euler characteristic conjecture.

348349.title: The generalized double-exclusion Alder conjecture
348349.statement:
Let $q_d^{(a)}(n)$ count partitions of $n$ into parts at least $a$ whose parts differ by at least $d$. For $1\leq b\leq d+2$, let $Q_d^{(b,-,-)}(n)$ count partitions of $n$ into parts congruent to $\pm b \pmod{d+3}$, excluding the parts $b$ and $d+3-b$. Define

$$
\Delta_d^{(a,b,-,-)}(n)=q_d^{(a)}(n)-Q_d^{(b,-,-)}(n),\qquad \Delta_d^{(a,-,-)}(n)=\Delta_d^{(a,a,-,-)}(n).
$$

**Generalized double-exclusion Alder conjecture.** Let $a,d$ be positive integers with $1\leq a\leq d+2$. Then for all $n\geq 1$,

$$
\Delta_d^{(a,-,-)}(n)\geq 0.
$$

This conjecture is proposed to extend the modified Alder inequality to arbitrary admissible $a$, after observing that the single-exclusion version can fail for $a\geq 4$. Its resolution is not given in the source.

350736.title: Polynomial removal threshold exceeds the homomorphism threshold for odd cycles
350736.statement:
For a graph $H$, let $\delta_\chi(H)$ and $\delta_{\hom}(H)$ denote its chromatic and homomorphism thresholds, and let $\delta_{\mathrm{poly\mhyphen rem}}(H)$ denote its polynomial removal threshold. For the odd cycle $C_{2k+1}$ with $k\geq 2$, **the odd-cycle removal-threshold conjecture.**

$$
\delta_{\mathrm{poly\mhyphen rem}}(C_{2k+1})>\delta_{\hom}(C_{2k+1})
$$

This would separate the polynomial removal and homomorphism thresholds for every odd cycle of length at least five; determining these thresholds is presented as an open problem in the surrounding discussion.

351456.title: Existence of isolated n-PTMCs in Γn
351456.statement: Let $\Gamma_n$ denote the graph considered in the paper, and let an isolated $n$-PTMC mean an isolated perfect total-multipacking code with parameter $n$. **Existence conjecture.** There exists an isolated $n$-PTMC in $\Gamma_n$ for every $n>2$. The supplied context describes an iterative construction for the case $n=2$ and suggests the higher-dimensional existence claim, but does not provide a resolution for all $n>2$.

352364.title: The strong negative vertical-connectivity conjecture for minimally vertically 4-connected matroids
352364.statement:
Let $k$ be a positive integer. A matroid $M$ is **minimally vertically $k$-connected** if it is vertically $k$-connected and $M\setminus e$ is not vertically $k$-connected for every element $e$ of $M$.

**Strong negative vertical-connectivity conjecture.** There is an infinite family of minimally vertically $4$-connected matroids with no $4$-cocircuits.

The known results establish the corresponding assertion for binary matroids in the opposite direction: every minimally vertically $4$-connected binary matroid with at least six elements has a $4$-cocircuit. Thus any examples predicted here must be non-binary; their existence is open.

352367.title: Infinite-family conjecture for minimally vertically k-connected matroids
352367.statement:
Let $k$ be an integer with $k\geq 4$. A matroid $M$ is **minimally vertically $k$-connected** if it is vertically $k$-connected and $M\setminus e$ is not vertically $k$-connected for every element $e$ of $M$.

**Infinite-family conjecture.** For each integer $k\geq 4$, there is an infinite family of minimally vertically $k$-connected matroids with no $k$-cocircuits.

This is presented as an extension of the conjectured $k=4$ construction and would give a negative answer to the paper's general question for every $k\geq 4$. It is open; the binary case is separately conjectured to behave oppositely for $k\geq 5$.

364485.title: Gao–Li conjecture on the Gao constant of finite non-cyclic groups
364485.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group. Write $|G|$ for its order and let $\mathsf{E}(G)$ denote its Gao constant, namely the least integer such that every sequence over $G$ of that length contains a product-one subsequence of length $|G|$. **Gao–Li's conjecture.** For every finite non-cyclic group $G$,

$$
\mathsf{E}(G) \leq \frac{3}{2}|G|.
$$

Han proved the conjecture for all finite non-cyclic nilpotent groups, and Gao, Li, and Qu proved the stronger bound $\mathsf{E}(G) \leq \frac{3}{2}(|G|-1)$ for finite non-cyclic groups of odd order greater than $9$. The conjecture remains open in general.
